messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — Hosted inference queue depth high for service `default-api` (triggered 1769994321). Symptoms: request latency spike (p95 > 2.5s), 502 errors increasing. Impact: some customers seeing timeouts. Paging oncall.
alex: ack, I'm on it. grabbing dashboard and logs now.
sam: joining. which pool is this hitting? dedicated or hosted shared?
alex: looks like hosted shared GPU pool in us-west-2. GPU utilization at 98% across pool.
maria: on dashboard: queue depth climbed from ~200 -> 320 in 3 minutes. autoscaler HPA showed no scale up after 175s.
jin: pasting HPA status from cluster:
```
$ kubectl get hpa service-default-api -o yaml
metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource:
      name: cpu
      target:
        averageUtilization: 60
status:
  currentReplicas: 10
  desiredReplicas: 10
  lastScaleTime: "2026-03-25T12:02:13Z"
  conditions: []
```
sam: that's odd — we use custom queue-length metric for autoscale in that deployment, not CPU. could this be an older HPA config? :thinking:
alex: I see an agent that pushes queue-length to custom metrics, but the HPA here references CPU. maybe config drift after last rollout.
maria: logs from autoscaler-controller showing "no scale target matched" around time queue spiked:
```
[12:01:58] controller: no metrics found for hpa/service-default-api, skipping
[12:02:12] controller: scale suppressed due to cooldown (window 300s)
```
jin: kube events show lots of PodEvicted events earlier — nodes hitting memory pressure. evicted: 3 pods in last 6m.
ops-bot: NOTE: Customer impact tag set to high-latency. Slack sig: #prod-impacted
sam: collecting node info now: `kubectl top nodes` shows GPUs memory at 99% and GPU utilization ~95%.
lisa: any recent model uploads or larger models pushed to hosted pool? warmup time could be causing requests to queue.
alex: yes — there was a model variant rollout 11:58 UTC that increased model size (quant->fp16 fallback) for accuracy tests.
maria: timeline so far:
 - 11:58 UTC: model rollout (large variant) started
 - 12:00 UTC: traffic spike on default-api (customer campaign)
 - 12:01-12:03 UTC: queue depth rises, HPA doesn't scale (wrong metric), nodes start evicting pods
 - 12:04 UTC: errors increase, oncall-bot page

sam: hypothesis tracker:
  H1: HPA misconfigured (CPU metric) -> no scale on queue-length
  H2: GPU pool saturated due to model rollout heavy warmup -> capacity reduced
  H3: Evictions from memory pressure amplified scale issues
  H4: Cooldown window prevented rapid scaling

jin: sharing relevant logs (trimmed):
```
[12:00:58] model-loader: starting load model-id=rm-large-v2
[12:01:10] model-loader: loading weights (size=16GB)
[12:01:45] kubelet: eviction threshold passed on node i-0f..., evicting pods
[12:02:10] hpa-controller: observed CPU 42% -> no scale
[12:02:50] request-router: queue-length=310, inflight=80, avg-rt=1.9s
```
alex: mitigation done in-flight: i) increased minReplicas to 15 for default-api, ii) enabled burst-capacity (+2 prewarmed nodes), iii) rolled back model variant for hosted shared at 12:08 UTC.
sam: after mitigations: queue depth dropped to ~40 by 12:12, error rate back to baseline by 12:14.
maria: customer impact estimate: ~7% of requests during 12:01-12:12 experienced >= 1 retry or 502. Affected tenants: 8 customers (one large enterprise had some timeouts on interactive endpoints).
lisa: good catch on rollback. we should capture warmup time per model so autoscaler can factor it in.
ops-bot: ACTION recorded: create postmortem doc in #incidents, assign owner, include timeline + metrics.
alex: immediate action items while still in-incident:
 - capture exact HPA YAML across clusters for default-api (sam)
 - export node logs for evicted nodes (jin)
 - run an audit for any recent rollout that touched HPA configs (maria)
 - quantify request retries per customer (lisa)

sam: posting HPA yaml snapshot:
```
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: service-default-api
spec:
  minReplicas: 10
  maxReplicas: 50
  metrics:
    - type: Resource
      resource:
        name: cpu
        target:
          type: Utilization
          averageUtilization: 60
```
sam: confirmed: HPA metric is CPU. config drift for queue-length rule happened in last deploy.
jin: node logs (snippet):
```
kernel: OutOfMemory: process oom-killer invoked
kubelet: Pod "model-loader" killed due to memory pressure
```
maria: leaning hypothesis ranking: H1 (metric drift) + H2 (warmup & model size) are primary; H3/H4 are secondary contributors.
alex: good. for the RCA doc we'll need: root cause statement, timeline, evidence (metrics and logs), action items (short/medium/long term), rollback/mitigation timeline, and owner.
lisa: medium-term mitigations I propose:
 - enforce HPA manifest lint in CI (prevent drift)
 - add queue-length custom metric as primary for model-serving HPAs
 - prewarm pool when large model rollouts happen (auto-warm hooks)
 - reduce HPA cooldown to 60s for critical endpoints

ops-bot: Handoff: alex -> sam for next 8 hours. sam will lead postmortem and coordinate follow-ups. :thumbsup:
alex: handing off with summary: rollback done, capacity bumped, nodes recovering. handoff notes posted to incident doc (link will follow).
sam: taking over. I'll assemble logs + dashboards and create the postmortem draft today. assigning action items and ETA for fixes.
jin: leaving logs export running; will attach S3 link in the postmortem doc.
maria: please tag infra and product for model rollout policy changes.
ops-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED (mitigated) at 1769994689. Root cause under investigation. Marking thread for postmortem drafting.
sam: final: we should run a tabletop for model rollout -> autoscale interactions. adding to backlog.
alex: thanks everyone. add me to the postmortem owner list as reviewer. :eyes:
